title: Learning image-based tree crown segmentation from enhanced lidar-based pseudo-labels
relevance: Trains an image-based crown segmentation model on pseudo-labels derived from airborne laser scanning and refined with SAM 2, at ZERO manual annotation cost, and reports outperforming available general-domain models on the task. This is the most direct alternative to annotation-plan item 1 (the ~1-3k hand-drawn 2020 crowns) that the loop has found: we already hold a 3DEP CHM and 7.5 cm optical imagery, and the CHM's ~2016 vintage is nearly contemporaneous with the 2016 Snohomish and 2017 CoE acquisitions, so pseudo-labels could be generated where the CHM covers (59.8% of the city) and the trained model applied everywhere. It also sidesteps the manual-label inflation problem of ID 165, since lidar-derived crowns are not correlated with an RGB model's errors the way hand-drawn ones are. PREPRINT, and its quantitative comparison against manually-annotated baselines is not stated in the abstract.

authors: Chen, M., Russell, D., Pallavoor, A., Young, D. & Wu, J.
title: Zero-shot tree detection and segmentation from aerial forest imagery
relevance: Evaluates SAM2 zero-shot for tree detection and segmentation and concludes it complements rather than replaces in-domain trained methods, working best when prompted by an existing detector. Read with the accompanying finding from this search - that training on COARSE OR NOISY labels is more robust than any current zero-shot option - it settles the ranking for our instance stream: pseudo-label-and-train beats zero-shot, and zero-shot is a refinement stage rather than a substitute for training. That is also a quiet endorsement of our existing noisy-label pipeline design, which trains on projected labels rather than waiting for clean ones.
